title: Complete Guide to Journalist & Whistleblower Privacy
metaDescription: Essential privacy tools and practices for journalists and whistleblowers to protect sources, communicate securely, and maintain anonymity.
intro: Protecting sources and maintaining secure communications is critical for journalists and whistleblowers. This comprehensive guide covers essential privacy tools, secure communication methods, and operational security practices to safeguard sensitive information and protect against surveillance.
prerequisites: Willingness to learn new communication tools
Understanding of the importance of source protection
Access to a computer or mobile device

steps.title: Establish Secure Browsing Habits
steps.description: Create a foundation of privacy-focused browsing to prevent tracking and surveillance of your research and communications.
actions: Install and configure Incognito Browser for enhanced privacy protection
Use Tor Browser for maximum anonymity when researching sensitive topics
Configure browser settings to block trackers and disable JavaScript when necessary
Use different browsers for different activities to compartmentalize your work
Clear browsing data regularly and use private/incognito mode consistently
steps.proTip: Incognito Browser provides built-in tracker blocking and privacy features that make it ideal for journalists conducting sensitive research.
steps.warning: Never use your regular browser for sensitive journalism work - always use privacy-focused tools.

steps.title: Set Up Encrypted Communication Channels
steps.description: Establish secure methods for communicating with sources and colleagues using end-to-end encrypted messaging platforms.
actions: Install Signal for encrypted messaging and voice calls
Set up ProtonMail or Tutanota for encrypted email communication
Configure disappearing messages in Signal for sensitive conversations
Create separate communication accounts for different stories or sources
Learn to verify encryption keys and contact authenticity
Set up Briar for decentralized messaging in high-risk situations
steps.proTip: Use Signal's registration lock feature and set a PIN to prevent SIM swapping attacks on your account.
steps.warning: Avoid using mainstream messaging apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS for sensitive communications.

steps.title: Implement Network Security Measures
steps.description: Protect your internet connection and hide your location from potential surveillance using VPNs and secure networks.
actions: Subscribe to a no-logs VPN service like ExpressVPN or NordVPN
Connect to VPN before any sensitive online activity
Avoid public WiFi for work - use mobile hotspot or VPN if necessary
Change your location frequently using different VPN servers
Use Tor over VPN for maximum anonymity when needed
Consider using a dedicated laptop for sensitive journalism work
steps.proTip: Test your VPN for DNS leaks regularly using tools like dnsleaktest.com to ensure your real location isn't exposed.
steps.warning: Free VPNs often log user data and should be avoided for journalism work.

steps.title: Configure Secure File Storage and Sharing
steps.description: Set up encrypted storage solutions and secure methods for receiving and sharing sensitive documents with sources.
actions: Install VeraCrypt for creating encrypted file containers
Set up OnionShare for anonymous file sharing
Use SecureDrop if your organization has it set up for receiving leaks
Configure encrypted cloud storage like Tresorit or pCloud Crypto
Learn to use GPG/PGP encryption for email attachments
Create secure backup procedures for sensitive materials
steps.proTip: Always encrypt files before uploading to cloud storage, even if the service claims to be encrypted.
steps.warning: Never store sensitive documents in plaintext or use mainstream cloud services like Google Drive for confidential materials.

steps.title: Establish Operational Security (OpSec) Protocols
steps.description: Develop systematic security practices to minimize risks and protect yourself and your sources from identification.
actions: Create separate identities and accounts for different investigations
Use burner phones and email addresses for sensitive communications
Meet sources in secure locations without surveillance cameras
Vary your routines and travel patterns when working on sensitive stories
Keep detailed security logs of your communications and meetings
Educate sources on basic security practices to protect themselves
steps.proTip: Consider using a code system or predetermined signals with sources to verify authenticity and indicate safety.
steps.warning: Assume all electronic communications can be intercepted - plan accordingly and use multiple layers of security.

steps.title: Secure Your Devices and Data
steps.description: Implement device-level security measures to protect against physical access and remote surveillance.
actions: Enable full-disk encryption on all devices using BitLocker (Windows) or FileVault (Mac)
Use strong, unique passwords and enable two-factor authentication everywhere
Install and configure a password manager like Bitwarden or 1Password
Keep operating systems and software updated with latest security patches
Disable location services and unnecessary permissions for apps
Use a security key for two-factor authentication on critical accounts
steps.proTip: Consider using a separate, encrypted USB drive for storing sensitive documents that you can physically secure or destroy if needed.
steps.warning: Never leave devices unattended in hotel rooms or other unsecured locations when traveling for stories.

faqs.question: What is SecureDrop and how does it protect whistleblowers?
faqs.answer: SecureDrop is an encrypted platform that allows whistleblowers to anonymously submit documents to journalists. It uses Tor network to hide the source's identity and provides end-to-end encryption to protect the content from interception.

faqs.question: Can I use regular email for communicating with sources?
faqs.answer: No, regular email is not secure for sensitive communications. It can be intercepted, monitored, and stored by various parties. Always use encrypted email services like ProtonMail or secure messaging apps like Signal.

faqs.question: How do I verify that my VPN is actually protecting my privacy?
faqs.answer: Test for IP, DNS, and WebRTC leaks using tools like whatismyipaddress.com, dnsleaktest.com, and browserleaks.com. Check that your real IP address and location are hidden when the VPN is active.

faqs.question: What should I do if I suspect I'm under surveillance?
faqs.answer: Immediately increase your security measures: use Tor browser exclusively, switch to new encrypted communication channels, avoid predictable patterns, and consider consulting with security experts or press freedom organizations.

faqs.question: Is it safe to meet sources in person?
faqs.answer: In-person meetings can be safer than digital communications if done correctly. Choose locations without cameras, vary meeting spots, use counter-surveillance techniques, and establish emergency protocols with your source.

faqs.question: How can I protect my sources' identity in my reporting?
faqs.answer: Remove or alter identifying details, use pseudonyms, avoid specific location references, store source information separately from story materials, and consider the timing of publication to avoid connecting sources to leaks.
